title: S&P Global Flash Germany PMI (Sep 2026) — 07:30 UTC / 03:30 ET, the largest single component, printing 30 minutes BEFORE the Eurozone aggregate it is weighted into
source: EST: two primaries, both fetched direct 2026-09-09 by the sp-global-flash-eurozone-pmi-2026-09-23 initial research. (1) S&P Global's forward PMI calendar, pmi.spglobal.com/Public/Release/ReleaseDates?language=en (HTTP 200, 23,858 bytes): 'September 23 ... 07:30 UTC S&P Global Flash Germany PMI'. (2) The publisher's own past-release archive, pmi.spglobal.com/Public/Release/PressReleases?language=en (HTTP 200, 92,883 bytes), shows the same slot actually delivered one month earlier: 'August 21 2026 07:30 UTC | S&P Global Flash Germany PMI'. 07:30 UTC is 03:30 ET under EDT. Filed estimate on the standing schema gap market-events-data.ts carries — no confirmed-source prefix covers a private PMI compiler — and because this lane never self-confirms an event it discovered in-sweep. Discovered in the never-assessed initial research of sp-global-flash-eurozone-pmi-2026-09-23, 2026-09-09
notes: PROPOSED BECAUSE IT IS THE MECHANISM THAT MAKES THE EUROZONE AGGREGATE LESS INFORMATIVE THAN ITS NAME. The proposing ledger's structural finding is that the 08:00 UTC Flash Eurozone PMI is substantially pre-announced by its own components: the publisher's methodology, quoted verbatim from its own August release PDF, is that 'Eurozone manufacturing and services indices are calculated by weighting together the national indices. National weights are calculated from annual manufacturing or services value added sourced from Eurostat' — and Germany, the largest of those national panels, prints 30 minutes earlier at 07:30 UTC, France 45 minutes earlier at 07:15. This is the same pre-announcement mechanic the sp-global-flash-us-pmi-2026-09-23 ledger established for flash-versus-final, operating inside a single morning instead of across twelve days. Without both components on the calendar, a future session cannot check that claim. NOT MEASURED: no first-hand bar work was done on the German print specifically. What WAS measured, on the aggregate and reported in the proposing ledger, is that the whole European block leaves no distinguishable footprint in US-hours instruments — the euro-minus-SPY residual at the US open ran above its own median in only 4 of 15 instrument-days against a 50% base rate across three flash days. So this entry is filed low on the same evidence and inherits the same caution: it is here to make a structural argument checkable, not because it is asserted to move a US window. DELIBERATELY NOT PROPOSED alongside it: Flash UK (08:30 UTC, not a Eurozone component), and the Eurozone finals on 2026-10-01 and 2026-10-05 — the publisher's own PDF publishes the flash-to-final gap as an absolute 0.3 on the composite, which is a receipt rather than an event, and filing every European print for a measured null would be adding noise to a calendar this research exists to keep honest. Cheap, dated, self-adjudicating falsifier: the release either lands 2026-09-23 at 07:30 UTC or it does not, settling in 14 days. Nothing here is a trade; estimate widens caution and licenses nothing
